text: Altar sites set up on hills and mountaintops. After the temple was built they easily became mixed with idol worship, and the prophets rebuked them again and again.
A sacrifice in which an animal was burned whole on the altar to God, expressing complete devotion.
Offerings expressing peace with God and thanks. Part was burned on the altar, and the rest was eaten together by those who brought it.
Worship in which animals or grain were offered to God, presented by priests at the appointed place.
A gold-covered wooden chest holding the stone tablets engraved with God's covenant. It showed that God was among his people.
The Bible's word for winged angels who guard God's presence. Their figures were carved above the ark and in the Most Holy Place.
The innermost and holiest room of the temple, where the ark was kept. Only the high priest could enter, once a year.
A holy place set apart for God; here, the temple.
The promise made between God and his people: God would protect them, and they would serve him alone.
The book recording the law God gave through Moses. It was found again in the temple in Josiah's day and read aloud.
The teaching and rules God gave Israel through Moses, the standard for worship and daily life.
Teachings God ordered his people to keep, centered on the Ten Commandments.
A person who received God's word and delivered it to kings and people.
A respectful title for a prophet sent by God.
Groups who gathered around a prophet to learn and live together. In the days of Elijah and Elisha there were several in different places.
To prophesy is to deliver the message a prophet received from God. It can foretell the future, but it is often a warning to turn back now.
A person who served between God and the people by offering sacrifices in the temple. Originally only Aaron's descendants from the tribe of Levi could serve.
The chief of the priests. Once a year he entered the Most Holy Place to make atonement for the people.
The tribe of Levi was set apart for the work of the temple. Jeroboam broke this rule and made anyone a priest.
One of the great clans of Israel descended from the twelve sons of Jacob. The nation was made up of twelve tribes.
Burning fragrant incense as an offering to a god. The rising smoke stood for prayer going up.
Precious fragrant resins and spices, costly goods carried by camel from far away.
A heavy unit of weight, about 34 kg. A talent of gold was a fortune.
A unit of weight and of money, about 11 g, used mostly to weigh silver.
A dry measure for grain, about 7 liters.
A god the Canaanites believed controlled rain and storms. His worship spread widely in Israel under Ahab and Jezebel.
A Canaanite goddess, worshiped through wooden poles or carved images set up as her symbol.
Standing stones set up as a mark of idol worship. The law said not to set them up but to break them down.
Images made of wood, stone, or metal and worshiped as gods. The Bible sees this as the sin of turning away from God.
A calf-shaped image made of gold. Worshiped in place of God, both in the wilderness and in Jeroboam's time, it became a great sin.
The bronze snake Moses put on a pole in the wilderness to save the people's lives. Later people worshiped it as an idol, so Hezekiah destroyed it.
A huge bronze water basin in the courtyard of Solomon's temple, holding water for the priests to wash.
God's great anger when he sees sin.
A remarkable event showing that what God has said is true.
A ceremony of pouring olive oil on someone's head to install a king or priest, meaning God had chosen and appointed that person.
Belonging to peoples other than Israel.
The whole people gathered in one place to worship God.
Wives of a king ranked below his official queens.
A wooden frame laid on the necks of two oxen so they could pull a plow or cart. It can also stand for a heavy burden or oppression.
Thought to be a very painful whip fitted with metal or barbs. It means ruling even more harshly.
A horse-drawn war cart, the strongest weapon of ancient armies.
Soldiers on horseback. 'The chariots and horsemen of Israel' meant the strength that protected the nation.
An attendant who stays close by to run errands and serve.
Two oxen sharing one yoke and pulling together as a team.
Clothing woven from rough hair, worn to show grief or repentance.
Going without food for a set time to cling to God, a sign of grief or repentance.
A wide, flat area where stalks of grain were beaten to loosen the kernels. Near a city gate it also served as a meeting place.
Tying up a long robe with a belt, getting ready to run or work.
A very quiet, gentle sound. Elijah met God not in the mighty wind but in a soft voice.
In the Bible, leprosy covered not only today's Hansen's disease but many serious skin diseases. Those who had it had to live outside the town.
A high-ranking general who led an army.
A thick timber laid across between posts to hold up a roof.
A small room behind a larger one, out of sight of others.
A person who kept watch from a wall or tower to guard the city.
A tall structure built for watching and guarding from far off.
The original word means sexual unfaithfulness outside marriage. The Bible often uses it as a picture of worshiping idols, being unfaithful to God.
Using magic such as spells and fortune-telling. The law forbade it.
Palace officials who served the king and queen closely.
Officers each leading about a hundred soldiers.
The seat where a king sits, standing for royal power.
Wealth paid every year to a stronger nation as a sign of submission.
An official in charge of writing and records. In this period it was a high office handling the palace's documents.
An official who recorded and announced the affairs of the palace.
The language of the Arameans. It was used by diplomats of many nations at the time, so ordinary people of Judah did not understand it well.
Words or actions that dishonor God or treat him with contempt.
A name for Jerusalem, especially the hill where the temple stood; the place where God dwells.
An angel sent by God to announce or carry out his will.
Israel's greatest festival, remembering the night of rescue from Egypt. Families killed a lamb and ate it together.
The leaders God raised up in times of crisis to guide Israel before there were kings.
People who claimed to call up the spirits of the dead to tell fortunes. The law strictly forbade it.
The commander of the troops who guarded the king.
Mounds of earth piled up to a city wall during a siege, so that siege weapons could be moved up them.
Great suffering and hardship.
